title: Warmfall Reserve and Soft Siege Protocol — PRD Draft
content:
Context and motivation:
We regularly see two related operational pain points for Dedicated customers: 1) sudden tenant demand spikes that exceed reserved capacity (microbursts / campaign-driven traffic) and 2) noisy-neighbor or emergent overload scenarios where a single tenant's traffic destabilizes a pool and forces broad throttling. Existing constructs (hard reserves + opportunistic burst credits) reduce cost but still result in slow cold starts, evictions, or heavy-handed throttles that harm latency-sensitive apps.

Idea summary (Warmfall + Soft Siege):
- Warmfall Reserve: a hybrid warm-pool + reserve buffer that bridges reserved capacity and on-demand soft capacity. Warmfall units are lightweight prepped slots (warm containers with KV prefetch + warmed cache indices) that can be owned by a specific tenant as short-duration leases. They are cheaper than fully reserved capacity but more expensive than pure shared burst. Leases are time-limited and releasable.
- Soft Siege Protocol: a tenant-protection mode activated when noisy behavior is detected (e.g., tail latency spikes, sustained queue growth, or token spam). Instead of immediate eviction, the pool transitions the tenant into graduated degradation lanes: reduced concurrency cap -> warmfall fallback -> routed to isolated sandbox with degraded QoS -> optional degrade to a lower-fidelity model. The idea is graceful handoff rather than forceful drop.

Goals:
- Reduce cold-start and latency penalty for burst events by 50% vs current opportunistic warm-pool baseline.
- Keep SLO compliance for unaffected tenants (P99 latency) within 10% delta in surge scenarios.
- Provide a predictable billing/credit model so customers understand cost tradeoffs for warmfall leases.

Non-goals:
- Not a wholesale replacement for dedicated reserved capacity commitments.
- Not intended to enable unlimited burst for small tenants—it's a controlled buffer.

Design overview:
1) Warmfall units and leasing model:
   - Warmfall unit: VM/container prewarmed with runtime and model weights (cold containers: ~20s start; warmfall: ~500ms to first token). Configurable prefetch for top-K KV cache items based on tenant profile.
   - Lease semantics: tenant can request warmfall credit via API or be auto-offered when predictive signals trigger. Each lease has: duration, cost-per-minute, and preemption-priority score. Leases can be queued and topped up.
   - Accounting: warmfall usage measured in unit-minutes; displayed in console with burn-rate smoothing. Billing ties to Dedicated plan with a separate line-item for warmfall vs burst tokens.

2) Soft Siege detection and lane transitions:
   - Signals: sustained >5x baseline qps over 1 minute, P95 latency above SLO, queue depth > threshold, anomalous token patterns. Signals come from per-tenant tracing + pool telemetry.
   - Lanes (in order):
     a) Gradual cap: reduce concurrency and concurrency burst window for tenant; short timer for recovery.
     b) Warmfall fallback: automatically try to allocate warmfall leases (if available); this maintains latency while reducing pressure on shared GPUs.
     c) Isolated sandbox: spin up an isolation slice (soft-sandbox) with reduced QoS and limited model fidelity; all new requests routed here until traffic normalizes.
     d) Model fidelity downgrade: if sandbox unavailable, route requests to a smaller/quantized variant to reduce GPU memory/throughput pressure.
   - Automatic recovery: tenant transitions back through lanes as signals normalize, with cooldown timers and a backoff multiplier on re-entry detection to avoid thrash.

3) Broker & admission control:
   - Central broker component that tracks warmfall supply, global pool headroom, and per-tenant priorities. Broker exposes admission API for runtime to request warmfall units and get preemption hints.
   - Admission policy configurable: priority-weighted, proportional-share, predictive-reserve (uses short-term forecast models to pre-allocate warmfall).

4) UX / API changes:
   - Console: warmfall dashboard (live headroom, per-tenant lease map, cost burn, predicted time to exhaustion).
   - API: POST /v1/dedicated/tenants/{id}/warmfall-lease {duration_minutes, max_concurrency} -> {lease_id, cost_estimate}
   - Alerts: default alert when warmfall burn > 75% or warmfall allocation success < 50% during surge windows.

Telemetry and observability:
- Key metrics: warmfall_units_available, warmfall_units_allocated, warmfall_burn_rate, tenant_siege_state, lane_transition_events, preemptions, P50/P95/P99 latency per lane.
- Traces: attach warmfall_lease_id to request traces; add lane tags for easy filtering in console.
- Evals: short synthetic spike tests to measure warmfall effectiveness across model families.

Operational playbook (sketch):
- Normal surge: broker auto-allocates warmfall; customers billed and notified; ops sees minor headroom dip.
- Siege onset: alerts fire for tenant_siege_state==soft_siege_active; runbook: notify SE + alert customer workspace, enable sandbox if not automatic, monitor degraded-lane latency.
- Preemption: if headroom exhausted and priority needed, warmfall leases with lowest priority_or_age are preempted with 30s notice; customer gets info via webhook.

Rollout plan / milestones:
- M0 (research): simulation of warmfall economics and latency curves (complete Q4 2025).
- M1 (alpha): broker + warmfall prototype, local tests (Q1 2026).
- M2 (beta): small cohort of Dedicated customers opt-in, add console and billing hooks (Q2 2026).
- M3 (ga): general availability with SLA clarifications and enterprise opt-in (Q3 2026).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: warmfall economics confuse customers -> Mitigation: clear console line-items + preflight cost-estimate API.
- Risk: thrash between lanes causing flapping -> Mitigation: cooldown timers, backoff multipliers, hysteresis in signal detection.
- Risk: warmfall preemption causing work loss -> Mitigation: 30s preemption notice and best-effort state checkpointing for common runtimes.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What is a reasonable default warmfall unit size across family of models (llama-like vs transformer-encoder)? (action: infra benchmarks)
- Billing: per-minute vs per-lease-bundle? (action: finance to model pricing tiers)
- How to surface warmfall preemption to customers gracefully in SDKs? (action: dx to propose SDK hooks)
- Implementation: should broker be centralized in control plane or distributed per-region? (action: SRE/infra architecture review)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally rough — focus feedback on: pricing model assumptions, lane ordering (is sandbox before fidelity downgrade?), and detection thresholds.
- Ping me in #prod-dedicated or schedule 30m sync if you'd like a demo of the spike sim.
